analysis.title: Taking Stock Of The Tech Unwind (Investor Positioning and Flows)
key_insights: DB downgraded Tech tactically to Neutral from Overweight on Oct 9 2026, warning of a V-turn down as relative performance, positioning and growth perception had become lop-sided. The market has moved fast since.
MCG & Tech underperformed the rest of the S&P 500 by 12pp over the last two weeks: Tech fell 7% while the rest of the S&P 500 rose 5%.

Tech relative performance is in the lower half of its long-run trend channel but about 5% above the channel bottom, from where it has reversed several times. In 2 of the last 5 rotations Tech overshot below the channel, driven by exogenous shocks (Liberation Day, Iran war).
Tech positioning fell to its lowest in 6 months and is near Iran-war lows. It dropped from the 85th percentile in early October to neutral (33rd percentile on the high-frequency measure).
Positioning in most other sectors rose this week but remains neutral to underweight. Energy is the exception, modestly above neutral (81st percentile).

Tech funds took in $30bn over two weeks as dip-buying, $12bn of it into leveraged ETFs, while other sectors saw $4.5bn of outflows. Thursday's selloff came with $1.5bn of Tech outflows. Unwinding of the dip-buying could prolong the selloff.

The last two Tech reversals higher coincided with strong earnings: late July off the channel bottom, and April's rebound out of the Iran-war selloff accelerated through earnings season. Another batch of key Tech earnings is due next week.

Tech positioning is now consistent with growth of about 10%, far below the 50% expected for Q3 and the 35% expected by the end of next year. Prevailing concerns are medium-term growth, cost of capital and policy/regulation, not near-term growth.
Next week's FOMC and the US mid-term elections the week after are key catalysts.

Overall equity positioning fell to neutral (0.02sd, 41st percentile). Discretionary positioning is -0.50sd (18th percentile), the lowest in over a month. Systematic positioning is 0.65sd (79th percentile), down but still overweight.
Large-cap positioning fell to modestly overweight (0.28sd, 59th percentile). Small-cap positioning fell sharply to -0.79sd (12th percentile), the biggest underweight since April 2023.

Systematic components remain elevated: vol-control allocation at the 81st percentile, risk-parity equity weight at the 81st percentile, CTA equity exposure at the 62nd percentile (SPX 87th, NDX 66th, RTY 30th). CTA bond exposure is at the 7th percentile.
Sentiment is washed out: AAII bearish sentiment is at the 91st percentile since 1987, bull-bear spread at the 21st percentile, and neutral at the 4th percentile.

Options flow is bullish: net call volume is at the 89th percentile since 2010 and the call/put ratio at the 57th percentile. L/S hedge fund beta to the S&P 500 is at the 86th (1m) and 88th (3m) percentile.

Sector positioning percentiles (high-frequency): Financials 20%, Energy 81%, Consumer Cyclicals 31%, Industrial Cyclicals 27%, Materials 25%, Staples 15%, Healthcare 50%, Real Estate 52%, Utilities 9%, Cyclicals 26%, Defensives 17%.
Announced S&P 500 buybacks are $192bn over 3 months in one chart and $209bn for the sector breakdown over the last 3 months.
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $358, 2027 EPS $420.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically downgraded to neutral on Oct 9. Positioning is now neutral and well below levels implied by earnings growth, and relative performance is near but above the channel bottom, so a rebound with earnings is possible.
Positioning is the only one modestly above neutral (81st percentile). This is a positioning observation rather than a rating.

earnings_insights: Consensus Q3 2026 blended earnings growth for large-cap MCG & Tech is about 50% (consensus), and about 35% by the end of next year (consensus). Tech positioning is consistent with only about 10% growth.
Another batch of key Tech earnings is due the week of Oct 26. DB notes the last two Tech reversals higher (late July, April) coincided with strong earnings releases.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cost of capital concerns make the FOMC a key catalyst for Tech.

tension_points.bull_case: Tech positioning is at a 6-month low and consistent with only about 10% growth versus 50% consensus for Q3. The last two reversals higher coincided with strong earnings, more Tech earnings are due next week, and $30bn of dip-buying shows underlying risk appetite.
tension_points.bear_case: Relative performance still has about 5% to fall to the channel bottom, and could overshoot on an exogenous shock. Unwinding of the dip-buying inflows (Thursday saw $1.5bn of outflows) could prolong the selloff, and concerns about the cost of capital, policy and regulation persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak batch of Tech earnings next week or a hawkish FOMC outcome would undercut the rebound case; a Tech relative performance break below the channel bottom would signal an overshoot.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tech was downgraded to neutral on lop-sided performance, positioning and growth perception, and has further relative downside of about 5% to the channel bottom, though positioning now looks washed out.
theme_stances.evidence: Tech positioning has slid to the lowest in 6 months

theme_stances.key_argument: Dip-buying inflows of $30bn into Tech funds could be unwound and prolong the selloff, but also show risk appetite for sharp V-turns higher.
theme_stances.evidence: Significant dip-buying in Tech over the last two weeks.
